stages.label: Planned
stages.meaning: Designed or on the roadmap. Not built yet.

stages.label: In development
stages.meaning: Being built now, or partly built.

stages.label: Implemented
stages.meaning: Built and passing automated tests. Waiting for hands-on review by the project owner.

stages.label: Verified
stages.meaning: The project owner has personally confirmed it working on a real homelab.

stages.label: Released
stages.meaning: Available to download in a public release.

milestones.title: Core Hearth interface
milestones.summary: Home, services, projects, to-dos, saved work, storage, and settings in one place, on desktop and phone.
milestones.detail: An earlier version runs every day on our own test homelab. Most pieces are still waiting for the owner's final hands-on sign-off.

milestones.title: Ember, the AI administrator
milestones.summary: Ember looks into problems with Hearth's own tools, explains what it found, and proposes fixes you approve.
milestones.detail: Works through Claude Code today. Ember never gets a shell, your files, or your passwords.

milestones.title: Service discovery and monitoring
milestones.summary: Finds the containers and apps on a machine, watches their health, and reads inside common apps like the *arr apps, Plex, and qBittorrent.
milestones.detail: Other machines are watched over the network today; deeper checks there are planned.

milestones.title: Guided first-run setup
milestones.summary: Create your account, connect an AI, and make Ember your own, in one guided flow that picks up where you left off.
milestones.detail: Account setup and personalization are built. The Connect your AI step is built and in review.

milestones.title: Choice of AI provider
milestones.summary: Use the AI you already have. Claude Code works today; Codex, OpenAI-compatible services, and local models through Ollama are planned.
milestones.detail: Each provider must be limited to Hearth's own tools before it is offered.

milestones.title: AI-assisted homelab planning
milestones.summary: Answer a few plain questions, let Hearth look at your computer (only if you say yes), and get a starter plan that fits it.
milestones.detail: Plans only for now: nothing is installed from a plan yet.

milestones.title: Approved installation and configuration
milestones.summary: Ember changes settings on your apps through plans you approve, with a backup, a check afterwards, and an automatic undo if it fails.
milestones.detail: A first set of app settings works today. Installing new apps and wiring them together is planned.

milestones.title: Secure credential management
milestones.summary: API keys and passwords live in an encrypted vault on your own machine. Ember uses them through Hearth without ever seeing them.
milestones.detail: Guided key setup exists for some apps; more are planned.

milestones.title: Automatic verification and recovery
milestones.summary: Every approved change is checked afterwards and undone on its own if it doesn't work.
milestones.detail: Built for today's repairs. Checking whole builds end to end is planned.

milestones.title: Public release
milestones.summary: A clean, documented install anyone can run on their own hardware.
milestones.detail: Not available to download yet. Follow along to hear when it is.

journey.title: Coming next: Ember builds your homelab
journey.intro: The goal: tell Hearth what you want, connect Ember, approve a plan, and watch Ember build and check a working homelab, without assembling it yourself.
